title: Apex tests, test data, isolation, `startTest/stopTest`, mocks, coverage, and meaningful assertions
objectives: Explain test isolation: tests do not see org data unless SeeAllData=true (discouraged).
Use Test.startTest/stopTest to run async and reset governor usage for the code under test.
Mock HTTP (and similar) instead of live callouts; assert behavior, not only coverage percent.
Cite official deployment coverage (75%) from the Apex Developer Guide without treating coverage as the goal.
diagnostic_question: A test uses SeeAllData=true, never calls startTest/stopTest around a Queueable, has no HttpCalloutMock, asserts System.assert(true), and boasts 80% coverage. What is wrong with isolation, startTest/stopTest, mocks, coverage, and assertions?
definition: Apex tests are @IsTest classes that deploy with your code. By default they cannot see org data—you insert synthetic LAB_ records (isolation). Test.startTest and Test.stopTest mark the tested work, reset governors for that block, and run queued async. HTTP callouts are mocked. Coverage of 75% is the official production-deploy floor, not a quality bar. Assertions must check data and behavior. ([Apex Testing](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing.htm); [Isolation of Test Data from Organization Data](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_data.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: Green tests that query production Accounts, skip stopTest, and assert true will pass CI and fail production. Interviewers want isolation, startTest/stopTest, mocks, and meaningful assertions—not a coverage screenshot.
sixty_second_explanation: Crash-test lab: you build dummy cars (test data), not steal street traffic (SeeAllData). startTest/stopTest is the timed crash window with a fresh governor budget and it releases the Queueable. Mocks are dummy walls so you do not need a real cliff. Coverage is how much of the chassis has sensors—75% is the legal minimum to leave the lab, not proof the dummy survived. Assertions are whether the dummy's belt held. Isolation means your dummies vanish when the test ends.
deeper_explanation: The Apex Testing topic requires tests before production deploy. @IsTest classes do not count against production Apex limits in the usual packaging sense. Tests should be deterministic. ([Apex Testing](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing.htm))

Isolation: tests do not have access to org data by default. Insert what you need. SeeAllData=true is documented but discouraged because org data changes and tests become flaky. You still cannot see some setup objects without SeeAllData—re-read Isolation of Test Data rather than inventing the list. ([Isolation of Test Data](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_data.htm))

Test.startTest() resets governor usage so setup DML does not starve the code under test. Test.stopTest() runs queued async (Queueable, future, batch in tests) and ends that fresh budget. The governors page notes that future/executeBatch inside start/stop do not count against queued-job limits the same way—cite that page, do not invent extra test-only numbers. ([Apex Testing](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Mocks: HttpCalloutMock + Test.setMock (APEX-013). You cannot make a real callout from a test without an allowed mechanism—default is mock. Coverage: 75% of Apex in the deployment plus coverage on every trigger is the official production deploy rule—reverify the exact wording on the current Testing / deploying topic. Coverage without assertions is theater.

Meaningful assertions: Assert.areEqual on LAB_ field values, row counts, exception types, Limits.getEmailInvocations, and mock call counts. System.assert(true) proves nothing. Test data factories must not hide DML-in-loop (APEX-018).

mental_model.analogy: A crash-test lab: dummy cars are test data, the timed window is startTest/stopTest, dummy walls are mocks, sensor coverage is the 75% floor, and belt measurements are assertions. You do not tow real street cars into the lab (SeeAllData).
useful_mapping: fresh instrument budget → governors reset at startTest
sensor coverage 75% → deploy floor, not quality
cars crushed then gone → isolation / rollback of test DML
where_it_breaks: Some setup objects still need special handling; read Isolation of Test Data.
stopTest runs async once; it is not a general 'commit'.
75% is org-deploy math, not per-method pride.

teach_back_prompt: Walk a failing production bug that tests missed because of SeeAllData, missing stopTest, no mock, 80% coverage, and assert(true).

review_schedule.prompt: What startTest/stopTest do to governors and async.
Two-minute interview: write a test plan aloud.

claims.claim: Apex tests are required to deploy to production. @IsTest methods exercise Apex. startTest/stopTest delimit the tested work and run queued async.
By default tests cannot access org data; they insert their own. SeeAllData=true is documented and discouraged for typical tests.
Callout tests use mocks (HttpCalloutMock). Live network is the wrong default.

Per-transaction governors still apply inside tests; startTest gives a fresh window. Official queued-job notes for future/executeBatch inside start/stop live on the governors page. Production deploy coverage is officially 75%—reverify the current testing/deploy sentence.

changed_in_release: Assert class APIs evolved; prefer System.Assert in new tests. Reverify the 75% deploy sentence on the current Testing topic for Summer '26.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact list of objects invisible without SeeAllData must be read from Isolation of Test Data.
Whether 75% is computed per-class or per-deployment set: re-read the current deploy topic; do not invent the rounding rule.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Tests insert LAB_ data; they do not SeeAllData by default. startTest/stopTest reset governors and run Queueable. Mock HTTP. 75% coverage is the deploy floor. Assertions must check outcomes, not true.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I write a factory that inserts isolated LAB_ rows. I startTest before the service, setMock if it callouts, stopTest before asserting async side effects. I runAs a standard user when the claim is security (APEX-015). I treat 80% coverage with assert(true) as a fail. I cite Isolation of Test Data and the Testing topic, and I reverify 75% wording on the deploy page.

when_to_use: When deploying Apex: you need tests, isolated test data, and the official 75% coverage floor.
When the code enqueues Queueable/future/Batch: wrap the invoke in startTest/stopTest before asserting.
When the code callouts: mocks via HttpCalloutMock, not a live named credential.
When proving security (APEX-015): runAs plus isolation, not SeeAllData admin queries.
When a test is flaky across orgs: remove SeeAllData and insert LAB_ rows.
When coverage is 80% but nothing is asserted: add meaningful assertions or the test is theater.
when_not_to_use: Do not use SeeAllData=true as the default for Apex tests.
Do not treat 75% coverage as proof the feature works.
Do not skip startTest/stopTest around async and then claim the Queueable was tested.
Do not call live HTTP from a unit test when a mock exists.
Do not assert(true) or assertNotEquals(null, null) as a coverage trick.
Do not use production customer rows as test data.

configuration_or_code: @IsTest static void reserve_ok() { LAB_Order__c o = LAB_Factory.order(); Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new LAB_AllocMock(200)); Test.startTest(); System.enqueueJob(new LAB_AllocQueueable(o.Id)); Test.stopTest(); Assert.areEqual('Reserved', [SELECT Status__c FROM LAB_Order__c WHERE Id=:o.Id].Status__c); }

interview_questions.question: How do Apex tests isolate data?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: By default they cannot see org data. I insert LAB_ rows. SeeAllData=true is documented and discouraged. Tests should pass in an empty scratch org.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Isolation of Test Data. I show a factory. I refuse Account LIMIT 1. I mention some setup objects are special-cased on that page—I will re-read rather than invent the list. Test DML rolls back; the class remains metadata.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Factory.order() inserts a LAB_Order__c the test owns.
tradeoffs: Portable scratch tests vs full-copy convenience

interview_questions.question: What do startTest and stopTest do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: startTest resets governors for the tested code. stopTest runs queued async and ends that window. Setup DML belongs before startTest. Assertions on Queueable belong after stopTest.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk a Queueable test aloud. I mention the governors page note that future/executeBatch inside the window have special queued-job counting—I will not invent the number. I do not call stopTest a commit.
interview_questions.example: startTest; enqueue LAB_AllocQueueable; stopTest; assert Status__c.

interview_questions.question: A test has 82% coverage and assert(true). Ship it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Coverage is the 75% deploy floor, not quality. I require assertions on outcomes. I add the missing 500 path even if coverage already passes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat coverage theater as a review fail. I ask which behavior would break in production unnoticed. I cite Testing topic purpose: verify behavior, not lines.
interview_questions.example: Catch block never entered; assert(true) at the end.

interview_questions.question: Queueable callout test throws CalloutException.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Missing Test.setMock, or setMock after the enqueue window, or a second callout without a multi-mock. Fix the mock; do not SeeAllData a token.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I register the mock before startTest, enqueue, stopTest, assert. I add a 500 mock method. I connect APEX-013. I do not disable tests.
tradeoffs: One mock vs chain of callouts
weak_answer_warnings: Putting a password in the test

interview_questions.question: How do you structure a test class for a service?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Factory methods, one behavior per test, start/stop around the invoke, runAs when security matters, mocks when integrations matter, assertions on LAB_ rows.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I avoid a 400-line test method. I name methods after outcomes. I keep SeeAllData off. I will mention @TestSetup for shared inserts with care about governor mixing. I do not hide DML-in-loop in the factory (APEX-018).
tradeoffs: One assert vs several related asserts
weak_answer_warnings: One test method for the whole class

interview_questions.question: Tests pass locally, deploy to prod validation fails coverage.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Production validation runs the suite against the deploy set. Uncovered triggers or excluded tests in the package cause 75% failure. I look at the coverage report, not the sandbox UI.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add tests for the uncovered trigger path with assertions. I do not add assert(true) fillers. I reverify whether the 75% math is per-deploy-set on the current page.
interview_questions.example: New LAB_ trigger with no test in the change set.
weak_answer_warnings: Lowering API version to dodge coverage

interview_questions.question: How do tests relate to governors and async job limits?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Inside startTest you get a fresh per-transaction allotment; caps still apply (100 SOQL, 10 sendEmail, 50 enqueue in sync). The governors page documents special counting for future/executeBatch inside start/stop. stopTest is when Batch/Queueable execute.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not claim tests disable governors. I arrange bulk data (200 rows) inside the window when proving bulkification (APEX-007/018). I cite the governors URL rather than a Trailhead round number if they disagree.
interview_questions.example: Insert 200 LAB_ orders before startTest; startTest; update them; stopTest; assert one SOQL in the trigger via Limits or debug.

interview_questions.question: When is SeeAllData acceptable?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the Isolation of Test Data topic says you cannot create that setup object in a test. Then I still assert, comment the reason, and minimize the query. It is never the default.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the Isolation page rather than memorizing an unofficial object list. I still prefer inserting what I can. I never SeeAllData to read customer Cases.
interview_questions.example: @IsTest(SeeAllData=true) only to query a Pricebook2 if the current Isolation page still requires it—Needs verification per API version.
